groups.reason: The handler calls itself a local-host shell escape hatch and executes with disabled permission profile and no sandbox.
groups.atlas_replacement: A typed tool operation may execute only after durable prepare/dispatch, structured policy, hard limits, and sandbox supervision.

groups.reason: The protocol documents unsandboxed spawn and the processor begins from the complete daemon environment.
groups.atlas_replacement: The sandbox supervisor owns a filtered per-operation process tree, stdin, PTY, output cap, deadline, cancellation, and cleanup.

groups.reason: The raw client method accepts permission overrides and flags that remove timeout and output bounds.
groups.atlas_replacement: Atlas exposes bounded operation commands whose clients cannot raise hard limits or choose broader sandbox profiles.

groups.reason: The raw methods accept absolute paths and invoke the executor filesystem with sandbox None.
groups.atlas_replacement: Descriptor-relative workspace tools enforce tenant root, structured read/write capability, symlink defenses, byte limits, audit, and sandbox.

groups.reason: These methods mutate host configuration, roots, imports, or enabled behavior outside an Atlas versioned policy transaction.
groups.atlas_replacement: Versioned configuration proposals require authorization, validation, durable audit, rollback, and policy-lint evidence.

groups.reason: Installation, checkout, upgrade, sharing, and deletion combine network, filesystem, code, and configuration side effects.
groups.atlas_replacement: Release one uses explicit user-approved package operations through provenance, egress, policy, isolated host, and audit gates.

groups.reason: OAuth, remote resources, and tool calls cross credential, network, extension, and output trust boundaries.
groups.atlas_replacement: Per-workspace isolated MCP hosts use opaque credentials, bounded pending calls, egress policy, result validation, and cleanup.

groups.reason: These operations mutate authentication, credits, messages, or upload data to an external service.
groups.atlas_replacement: Provider credentials and all outbound data use configured credential handles and the Atlas egress/cost/audit gateway.

groups.reason: Remote control changes the control-plane trust boundary and environment creation can trigger external account or compute effects.
groups.atlas_replacement: Release one is local-only; remote mutual TLS and environment provisioning remain non-goals until separately approved.

groups.reason: Realtime sessions add continuous provider egress, audio privacy, streaming, and cost surfaces outside release-one requirements.
groups.atlas_replacement: No realtime RPC is registered in release one.

groups.reason: The lifecycle semantics are useful, but Atlas requires authenticated grants, idempotency, append-before-project state, pagination, and reconnect sequences.
groups.atlas_replacement: Atlas-owned versioned protocol and journal implement compatible concepts without exposing the upstream handlers.

groups.reason: Approval UX is reusable as a concept, but an Atlas receipt must bind authenticated actor, exact request hash, scope, expiry, and policy version.
groups.atlas_replacement: Durable allow/ask/deny policy and scoped approval receipts.

groups.reason: Atlas needs provider-neutral capability, health, region, data policy, usage, and price revisions without exposing provider credentials.
groups.atlas_replacement: Bounded paginated Atlas catalog and explainable router projections.

groups.reason: Read-only methods still expose host paths, configuration, extensions, repository content, or remote comparison state.
groups.atlas_replacement: Narrow paginated discovery and repository tools require current workspace authorization, byte limits, provenance labels, and audit.

registration_rule: Atlas registers only Atlas-owned methods. Any compatibility alias must name one reimplemented method, satisfy every required gate, and must not intersect a deny group. Unlisted upstream methods inherit default deny.
